name: Corner Strike
change: A chipped corner with cracks spreading from it and short arcs around the strike; two light hairlines elsewhere.
good: The clearest story: something struck the corner and the glass held. The corner carries the drama while the rest of the slab stays calm, with two faint hairlines.
watch: The busiest corner; on a smaller window the fracture takes a larger share of the panel.

name: Hairline Age
change: A small chipped corner and three or four long, faint hairlines, like old glass under strain.
good: The quietest: the slab looks old and strained rather than broken, and the long hairlines catch the light as the pointer moves.
watch: Faint at normal size, and the long hairlines are the most likely to pass behind text, though lightly.

name: Split Corners
change: Fractures at two opposite corners, one larger than the other, and a hairline between them.
good: Frames the panel: damage at two opposite corners balances the slab, like a pane that was dropped.
watch: Twice the corner detail; on every main window it could start to read as a pattern.

name: Edge Chips
change: A chipped corner and two small chips knocked from the rim, each with a short crack running in; one hairline.
good: Wear on the thick rim rather than a broken pane: small nicks with short cracks, the least dramatic damage.
watch: The small chips can read as marks or notches at a glance, and they sit along edges where titles and buttons go.

name: Deep Fracture
change: Fewer, longer breaks that run deep into the slab, seen as soft fracture planes inside the glass.
good: The most like a real break in thick glass: long, nearly straight fractures with soft planes inside the slab, and the strongest flash as the light moves.
watch: The largest marks: its long cracks reach well into the panel, behind its content.
